From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@serenatek.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-21T15:40:00Z
Subject: Status update: transient 500 spike affecting hosted generation (May 21)

Jordan —

We're reaching out with a brief update: between 15:05–15:14 UTC today we observed an elevated rate of 500 (internal server) responses for requests to our hosted generation endpoints in the us-west-1 region. Your integration logs indicate a small number of failed calls during that window.

What happened (interim):
- A deployment wave coincided with increased memory pressure on a subset of inference hosts; this caused request failures while autoscaling reacted.
- We detected the problem via alerting and rolled back the rollout and increased autoscale headroom.

Customer impact: some requests returned HTTP 500; retries with exponential backoff succeeded in most cases. No user data was exposed and request payloads were not lost — we did not observe partial generations.

What we did: rollback + hotfix to reduce memory footprint, raised headroom, and validated recovery. The platform returned to baseline by ~15:30 UTC.

Next steps:
- We are conducting a short post-incident analysis and will share a concise follow-up with root cause and remediation items within 24 business hours.
- Recommendation for clients: add a 250–1000ms jittered exponential retry for 5xx responses during transient spikes (we'll link to a sample snippet).

Links: status page — https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RED-2028-05-21-500-spike
Ticket: JIRA-RED-1189

If you'd like a quick sync to walk through your logs, I can set up 30m with our on-call.

Apologies for the disruption — we know reliability matters.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Customer Reliability Engineer

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-22T10:05:00Z
Subject: Post-incident update: 500 spike — root cause and remediation

Folks —

Summary of findings (triage complete):
- Root cause: a flawed memory estimator in the new kernel selection logic caused suboptimal placement on a subset of hosts during the rollout, which under a particular request-size distribution produced memory pressure and transient OOM-handling paths that returned 500s.
- Mitigation taken: the rollout was rolled back, a hotfix to the estimator was applied, and autoscale thresholds were temporarily increased to add headroom.
- Impact: limited; ~0.6% of requests in us-west-1 over the 9-minute window returned 500. Recovery validated by metrics and traffic tests.

Action items (short):
1) Backport estimator fix to the stable branch and add unit tests covering request-size edge cases. Owner: Runtime Team (Kim). ETA: 3 business days.
2) Add a short-circuit fallback to prefer conservative kernel choices during rollout windows. Owner: Runtime/Serving. ETA: 2 weeks.
3) Update public post-incident note on status.redwood.ai with root cause and mitigations. Owner: Incident Comms (Marissa). ETA: today EOB.

Jordan: on retries — safe provided you include an idempotency token or dedupe by request-id; we will follow up with a small code snippet you can plug in.

I'll close the incident in JIRA once the comms update is live.

Thanks all for the quick response.

Sean
